provenance.origin: Follow-up shape of the #1238 incident: the model asserted the WORKFLOW-TO-ACTION input mapping instead of the action's own declaration - it claimed the workflow names its credential input `ai-key` while the reviewed workflow passes `ai-api-key`, so GitHub would drop the workflow's credential. The reviewed repository's own workflow file (the workflow-side witness, read at the exact reviewed head) is a POSITIVE witness only: it corroborates the names that file's DIRECT action step passes and it never establishes an absence, so it never refutes the fabricated name. The claim is therefore unknown evidence and the review does NOT approve. Sanitized: repository, endpoint, model, and secret names replaced with placeholders; the pinned upstream action reference and the workflow skeleton are kept as factual citations of the incident shape.

name: AI PR Review

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, ready_for_review, labeled]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  checks: read

jobs:
  ai-review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out the pull request head
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - name: Run the AI review
        uses: misospace/pr-reviewer-action@5b1839535748f3afd1bd3ef04e8009302cba9aa6 # v3.7.0
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ai-base-url: ${{ secrets.AI_ENDPOINT }}
          ai-api-format: openai
          ai-model: review-model
          ai-api-key: ${{ secrets.MINIMAX_API_KEY }}

The workflow names its credential input under an input name the pinned action does not declare, so GitHub drops it.

## Findings

- **Major** (.github/workflows/ai_pr_review.yaml:32) - the workflow's credential input is named `ai-key`, so GitHub drops the action's credential.

## Recommendation

Request changes: rename the credential input.
